subject: Mathematics

book.title: Ganita Prakash
book.sourcePolicy: Chapter titles/order and high-level curriculum scope only; KirthiVerse teaching text, examples, hints and assessments must be independently authored.

chapter1Topics.title: Number patterns and sequences
competencies: identify a consistent pattern rule
extend a sequence
represent a pattern numerically or visually
explain reasoning in own words
misconceptions: treating a coincidence between two terms as a valid rule
confusing a term position with its value

chapter1Topics.title: Patterns in shapes
competencies: identify a visual construction rule
translate visual growth into counts
predict later stages
distinguish equal totals from equal constructions
misconceptions: using counts alone without describing the construction
copying a picture without identifying the repeatable transformation

chapter1Topics.title: Patterns in nature and everyday life
competencies: identify repeat units
distinguish repeating and growing patterns
model observations mathematically
test a proposed rule without overstating evidence
misconceptions: assuming every observed natural form follows an exact sequence
claiming a general rule from too few observations

chapter1CompletionRule: CHAPTER1_KIKI_TEACHING_SLICE_COMPLETE requires all three mapped topics to have independently authored teaching content, worked examples, linked practice/assessment, misconception handling, remediation/mastery evidence, deterministic QA, offline coverage and release regression coverage.

chapter2Topics.title: Points, line segments, lines and rays
competencies: distinguish geometric primitives by endpoint and extension properties
name segments, lines and rays consistently
interpret finite drawings as representations of ideal objects
recognise collinear points
misconceptions: classifying by drawn length instead of defining properties
reversing ray names without changing the endpoint
treating arrowheads as endpoints

chapter2Topics.title: Angle comparison and classification
competencies: identify vertex and arms
compare angles by amount of turn
classify acute right obtuse straight reflex and complete angles
use benchmark turns without relying on orientation
misconceptions: longer arms make a larger angle
a tilted right angle stops being right
the apparent area between arms defines angle size

chapter2Topics.title: Measuring and drawing angles
competencies: align and read a protractor from the correct zero
measure and construct angles in degrees
reason about reflex angles from a full turn
verify an angle bisector by equal measures
misconceptions: always reading one printed protractor scale
ignoring vertex-centre alignment
treating a visual midpoint as proof of an angle bisector

chapter2CompletionRule: CHAPTER2_KIKI_TEACHING_SLICE_COMPLETE requires all three mapped topics to have independently authored teaching content, worked examples, linked practice/assessment, misconception handling, remediation/mastery evidence, deterministic QA, lazy runtime integration, offline coverage, release regression coverage and a separate synthetic school-needs validation artifact. The school-needs artifact is deterministic readiness evidence only and does not establish live-school efficacy, attainment or school-specific pacing.

chapter3Topics.title: Number relationships, comparison and number-line structure
competencies: compare large numbers from place value
reason from stated local-neighbour conditions
derive equal number-line interval values from labelled anchors
place and estimate large values on a number line
misconceptions: comparing numbers from visual digit appearance rather than place value
ignoring which neighbours are included in a local comparison rule
assuming every equally spaced number-line mark increases by one

chapter3Topics.title: Digit sums, reversals, palindromes and repeatable number processes
competencies: analyse place value while rearranging digits
calculate and compare digit sums
recognise palindromes
execute a fixed digit algorithm accurately
separate observed patterns from universal proof
misconceptions: digit sum uniquely identifies a number
leading zeroes create new place value after reversal
many successful examples prove a rule for every starting number

chapter3Topics.title: Mental computation, numerical patterns, estimation and conjectures
competencies: decompose and compensate for mental calculation
explain useful numerical patterns
make and check reasonable estimates
distinguish conjecture from theorem
describe repeatable game strategies rather than lucky moves
misconceptions: an estimate must equal the exact answer
a shortcut needs no mathematical explanation
extensive testing automatically proves a conjecture
one successful move is a winning strategy

chapter3CompletionRule: CHAPTER3_KIKI_TEACHING_SLICE_COMPLETE requires all three mapped strands to have independently authored teaching content, worked examples, five linked assessments per lesson, misconception handling, remediation/mastery evidence, deterministic QA, lazy assessment loading, offline precache coverage, release-regression coverage and a separate synthetic school-needs validation artifact. The school-needs artifact is deterministic readiness evidence only and does not establish live-school efficacy, attainment or school-specific pacing.

chapter4Topics.title: Collecting, organising and counting data
competencies: frame a clear data question
organise raw observations with tally marks
construct and verify frequency tables
make conclusions bounded to the collected dataset
misconceptions: confusing a data value with its frequency
losing or double-counting observations
assuming the largest-looking category label has the largest frequency
generalising a small dataset to everyone

chapter4Topics.title: Pictographs and representation keys
competencies: read a pictograph key before interpreting symbols
convert symbol counts to frequencies
choose a practical symbol value
verify a pictograph against its source table
misconceptions: assuming one symbol always means one item
treating decorative symbol size as quantity
changing the key between categories
ignoring the meaning of a partial symbol

chapter4Topics.title: Bar graphs, scale and fair visual comparison
competencies: read and choose a consistent numerical scale
calculate bar height from value and scale
construct labelled zero-based bar graphs
detect misleading baselines or inconsistent axis intervals
misconceptions: reading grid-square count as the frequency regardless of scale
changing scale midway
drawing bars from different baselines
trusting apparent bar size without checking axis labels
